## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A 2.1 failure that works on TestFlight but fails in review is commonly attributed (community answer, Mar 2026) to hardcoded IPv4 literals or raw BSD sockets on the IPv6-only review network; use hostnames and URLSession/Network framework, and reproduce with an Internet Sharing NAT64 network. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-01) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/818386 · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/49979
- [statement] Guideline 2.3.1 prohibits hidden, dormant or undocumented features and requires new functionality to be described specifically in Notes for Review; generic descriptions are rejected. An optional user-keyed AI feature or Slack/SMTP alerting that a reviewer cannot trigger must be documented there. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/does-apple-review-check-your-server-side-code
- [statement] If a demo account cannot be supplied for legal or security reasons, 2.1 allows a built-in demo mode that shows full functionality, with prior Apple approval. For optional features needing user-supplied credentials, the safe pattern is that the core app works with none and the optional feature has a clearly labelled, documented off state. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/does-apple-review-check-your-server-side-code
- [statement] Apple does not publish App Review source IP ranges; blog reports of Cupertino or Sacramento ranges are unconfirmed and change, so allowlisting or geo/IP gating a backend is an antipattern for review. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-01) — https://ptkd.com/journal/does-apple-review-check-your-server-side-code · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Guideline 2.5.5 requires apps to be fully functional on IPv6-only networks, and Apple DTS states App Review tests on an IPv6-only network with DNS64/NAT64 (ARNAT64), which now behaves much like MacNAT64 (Internet Sharing based) rather than a carrier network. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/49979

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Guideline 2.1 tells developers to submit final builds, include demo account info if the app has a login, and turn on the back-end service so it is live and accessible during review; non-obvious features must be explained in Review Notes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://ptkd.com/journal/does-apple-review-check-your-server-side-code
- [statement] Apple staff caution that a rejection message citing IPv6 may have nothing to do with the network; crashes during review are bugs regardless of network state. Treat the network as one hypothesis, not the diagnosis. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/49979 · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS · also: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/48314
- [statement] Apple's published guidelines state no macOS version used by reviewers; macOS 27 shipped on 2026-09-14 per press reports, so the safest assumption is that the build must launch cleanly on the current release and the minimum deployment target. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02) — https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ · keywords: Review-environment reality: reviewer first launch on a clean account network and latest macOS
